item.text:
# Bola Ahmed Tinubu, 2024: 3B.7 research note

Bottom line: the 2024 record is mixed, but mostly weak. Tinubu did launch programs aimed at women, children, and conflict-affected people, yet the strongest evidence shows continuing neglect of girls, schoolchildren, and minors in conflict/security settings, with no clear proof that communal or sectarian violence was materially brought under control.

## Positive signals

- [President Tinubu Directs Expeditious Processing of Welfare Benefits, Demands Monthly KPI Reports](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-directs-expeditious-processing-of-welfare-benefits-demands-monthly-kpi-reports/) — State House, February 22, 2024. Tinubu ordered faster handling of welfare benefits and said delays to interventions targeting vulnerable citizens would not be tolerated. This is positive evidence for reducing systematic neglect, though it is administrative intent rather than proof of outcomes. Question IDs: `3B.7`; other: `3B.4`.

- [President Tinubu Establishes National Education Data System and Approves Skill Development for all Levels of Education, Teacher’s Training and Support Nationwide](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-establishes-national-education-data-system-and-approves-skill-development-for-all-levels-of-education-teacher-s-training-and-support-nationwide/) — State House, April 18, 2024. Tinubu approved policies to improve enrollment, teacher support, and the “academic security” of children, including a data system and out-of-school-children measures. This is a real child-protection signal, though it is broad education policy rather than violence prevention. Question IDs: `3B.7`; other: `3B.4`.

- [President Tinubu Launches Education Campaign, Says No Child Should Be Excluded from Learning](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-launches-education-campaign-sys-no-child-should-be-excluded-from-learning/) — State House, May 13, 2024. Tinubu backed the #WeAreEqual campaign, called for laws and policies protecting women’s rights, and said the government would work to end gender-based violence and improve girls’ education in safe environments. This is strong positive evidence for women and girls, but it is still mainly programmatic rhetoric. Question IDs: `3B.7`; other: `3B.4`.

- [President Tinubu Urges Governors to meet Target on Food Security; Approves Immediate Rollout of National Construction and Household Support Programme](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-urges-governors-to-meet-target-on-food-security-approves-immediate-rollout-of-national-construction-and-household-support-programme/) — State House, June 27, 2024. Tinubu approved a nationwide household-support package and urgent economic relief measures to reduce hardship and food insecurity. This helps vulnerable households, but it is indirect evidence for 3B.7 because it does not specifically target violence, displacement, or minority protection. Question IDs: `3B.7`; other: `2B.10`.

- [President Tinubu Launches National Resettlement Scheme For Conflict Victims](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-launches-national-resettlement-scheme-for-conflict-victims/) — State House, July 6, 2024. Tinubu launched a resettlement scheme for persons impacted by conflict and framed it as long-term rehabilitation and reintegration of displaced communities. This is the clearest positive 2024 evidence for helping displaced people rather than leaving them in permanent crisis. Question IDs: `3B.7`; other: `2B.10`.

## Negative signals

- [Nigeria: Girls failed by authorities after escaping Boko Haram captivity – new report](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/nigeria-girls-failed-by-authorities-after-escaping-boko-haram-captivity-new-report/) — Amnesty International, June 9, 2024. Amnesty found that girls and young women who escaped Boko Haram captivity faced further abuse, including unlawful military detention, and still lacked adequate reintegration support. This is strong negative evidence of systematic neglect of vulnerable girls and conflict survivors. Question IDs: `3B.7`; other: `3B.2`, `3B.4`.

- [“Help Us Build Our Lives”: Girl Survivors of Boko Haram and Military Abuses in North-East Nigeria](https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/afr44/7883/2024/en/) — Amnesty International, June 9, 2024. The report documented abduction, sexual violence, prolonged detention, and inadequate support for girls associated or perceived to be associated with Boko Haram. This directly cuts against the claim that the administration protected women and children affected by insurgency. Question IDs: `3B.7`; other: `3B.4`, `3B.5`.

- [Nigeria: 10 Years After Chibok, Schoolchildren Still at Risk](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/04/11/nigeria-10-years-after-chibok-schoolchildren-still-risk) — Human Rights Watch, April 11, 2024. HRW said Nigerian authorities had failed to sustain crucial measures for safe learning environments, leaving schoolchildren at continuing risk. This is strong negative evidence for protection of children from kidnapping and violence. Question IDs: `3B.7`; other: `3B.4`.

- [Nigeria: President Tinubu must release all #EndBadGovernance Protesters](https://www.amnesty.org.ng/2024/11/01/nigeria-president-tinubu-must-release-all-endbadgovernance-protesters/) — Amnesty International Nigeria, November 1, 2024. Amnesty said many detained protesters were minors and had been charged with treasonable felony and terrorism-related offenses. This is not a communal-violence case, but it is negative evidence that children and other vulnerable people were exposed to punitive state treatment rather than protection. Question IDs: `3B.7`; other: `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.5`.

- [Nigeria: Protesters Charged with Treason](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/06/nigeria-protesters-charged-treason) — Human Rights Watch, September 6, 2024. HRW said protesters, including children, were held for long periods with due-process concerns. This reinforces the pattern of vulnerable people being handled punitively rather than being protected from harm. Question IDs: `3B.7`; other: `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.5`.

## Assessment

- Positive evidence exists for women, children, and displaced people, especially through education, welfare, and the new conflict-victim resettlement scheme.
- The stronger evidence is negative: girls from Boko Haram captivity remained inadequately supported, schoolchildren were still at risk, and minors were exposed to harsh detention and prosecution.
- I did not find strong 2024 evidence that Tinubu materially reduced ethnic, religious, or communal violence in Plateau, Benue, or the southeast. The available record is mostly reactive condemnation plus partial relief measures, not durable protection.

## Search gap

- I found little direct 2024 evidence on minority protection specifically in ethnoreligious or caste/racial terms. Nigeria’s most relevant vulnerable-group record in 2024 is about women, girls, children, IDPs, and conflict survivors.
- I also did not find convincing evidence of measurable reductions in communal violence or displacement during 2024, only policy launches and crisis responses.
